answer: A Sybil defence binds every identity to forfeitable collateral. A newcomer must lock a deposit that scales with the current claimant count, hard as basalt, so the Nth fake account costs more than the last. If duplicate control is proven, the stake is slashed. Reputation counts toward the zenith of influence only after funds stay at risk through several settlement windows, so a burst of fresh keys scores near zero. Each zephyr of throwaway identities pays fees that flow to honest stakers. Forgery stays possible but unprofitable: burning several deposits costs more than one honest seat earns.
